narrative.title: The Maintenance Window Merger
narrative.scenario: A datacenter keeps an ordered list of non-overlapping maintenance windows. Ops files one new window that may overlap several existing ones. The calendar tool walks the sorted list: it copies every window that ends before the new one starts, absorbs every window it collides with by stretching the new one, and finally slots the (possibly enlarged) window before whatever remains.
narrative.inputFormat: A sorted non-overlapping list of intervals and a newInterval [start, end].
narrative.outputFormat: Return the merged, still-sorted, non-overlapping interval list.
constraints: intervals is sorted by start and non-overlapping

testCases.explanation: [4,8] swallows [3,5], [6,7] and [8,10] into one stretched window.
[2,5] merges with [1,3] and stays clear of [6,9].

starterCode.python:
def insert_interval(intervals, new_interval):
    result = []
    for start, end in intervals:
        if end < new_interval[0]:          # current ends before new begins
            result.append([start, end])
        elif new_interval[1] < start:      # new ends before current begins
            result.append(new_interval)
            new_interval = [start, end]
        else:                              # overlap: widen the new one
            new_interval[0] = min(new_interval[0], start)
            new_interval[1] = max(new_interval[1], end)
    result.append(new_interval)
    return result

hintLevels: Level 1: Three-way branching per interval: strictly before, strictly after, or overlapping.
Level 2: On overlap, stretch the pending interval instead of appending anything yet.
Level 3: Don't forget the final append — the pending interval flushes after the loop ends.
